THIS FILE IS STEP 1 OF tools/loop/ITERATION-PROMPT.md AND IT MUST STAY READABLE IN ONE Read.
STEP 1 READS THREE FILES, NOT ONE: this file, GATES.md, and PLAN.md §14. All three go through a Read
that has TWO ceilings: it TRUNCATES past 25,000 tokens and FAILS OUTRIGHT past 256 KB. BOTH HAVE
ALREADY BITTEN THIS FILE. iter127 hit the byte ceiling - the Read was refused, 459 KB, because the
`done` log had reached 397 KB of it. iter128 found the TOKEN cap had been truncating for longer and
unnoticed: at 74,115 bytes / 31,303 tokens, step 1 returned lines 1-43 of 92 and dropped `decisions`
(the six outstanding decisions), `doneCount`, `doneArchive`, `doneRecent` and `spikes`.

CORRECTED AT ITER129, because a later method depends on it: TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT. The tool prints
"[Truncated: PARTIAL view - showing lines 1-462 of 1500 total (68900 tokens, cap 25000)]". iter128
called truncation "the worse failure because it looks like success"; the real risk is an agent
SKIMMING PAST an explicit notice, not the tool hiding anything. That notice is also the ONLY tokenizer
on this machine (no tiktoken, no anthropic, no transformers), and it is how iter129 calibrated the
size checker: build a file over the cap but under 256 KB, Read it whole, divide bytes by the reported
total. Markdown measured 2.604 B/tok, this file's JSON 2.368.

RUN `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` AFTER EVERY EDIT TO THIS FILE, TO GATES.md, OR TO PLAN.md.
It measures ALL THREE step-1 files (iter128's version measured only this one), prints each file's
HEADROOM IN KB before it truncates, distinguishes the two ceilings, lists this file's largest fields,
flags every other tools/loop file, and EXITS NON-ZERO when something stops fitting.
WHEN IT TRIPS ON THIS FILE: move an append-heavy field into an archive under tools/loop/ and leave a
short pointer behind. There are SEVEN precedents - `doneArchive`, `blockersArchive`, `gatesArchive`,
`methodNotes`, `scratchInventory`, `spikesArchive`, and `decisions._archive` (iter130, the one that
keeps its pointer INSIDE the field it drained rather than as a sibling key) - and each one asserted
its round-trip before this file was rewritten. Do not discard content to make the check pass. WHEN IT TRIPS ON GATES.md OR
PLAN.md: that content is the spec and the gate instructions, so archive a settled section, never drop
one.

AND NOTE WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS AT THE TOP OF THE FILE RATHER THAN NEXT TO `doneArchive`: a truncated
Read still shows it. iter127's rotation rule was correct and had no effect, because it was written
into a field that sat past the cut. A rule that keeps a file readable is worthless in the half that
gets cut off.

**RUN `dotnet build` AND `dotnet test` BEFORE YOU CHANGE ANYTHING, AND AGAIN AFTER YOUR LAST WRITE.** iter132 found the suite red at HEAD with two commits on top of it. Several tests sweep the tree's own prose (RepositorySlugTests over *.md/*.yml/*.json outside `tests/` and `tools/`, QuickstartTests over fenced commands), so a docs-only edit — GATES.md included — can turn it red. iter139 opened and closed green at 1375/1375, 0 skipped.

FIVE MILESTONE GATES ARE OPEN AND ALL FIVE ARE MIRKO'S**, plus FIVE side items (paste-rule-8-2a, paste-force-push-hook, settings-corrections, paste-format-on-edit-hook, and NEW AT ITER139 restart-loop-driver) — ten unchecked boxes. One line each in `gates`; full instructions in GATES.md. A ticked box is the only thing that turns this loop back into a working loop. Cheapest first: restart-loop-driver (three commands), gate-m3 (add one `approved` label), gate-m4 (write one wrong comment), gate-m5 (answer decisions.m5Acceptance), gate-m2 (walk the 44 pages), gate-m6 (push main, then tag v0.1.0).

**READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH tools/loop/docume-loop.sh — iter139.** THAT FILE IS THE ONE THING AN ITERATION CAN EDIT BUT CANNOT MAKE TAKE EFFECT. The running driver started 2026-07-24 14:38:30 and bash parsed its `while` loop then; it is 56.6 h older than the file's newest commit, and BOTH commits since (c6fbf1e, 7de6a86 — iter137's whole deliverable) are dead code until Mirko restarts it. **So before you 'fix' anything in the driver, check whether your fix is already there and simply not running.** Live despite this, because they are re-read by path every pass: ITERATION-PROMPT.md and loop-settings.json. Inert for the same reason as the driver: tools/loop/MODEL. Re-runnable in ~2 s: `python3 .mtk/paths-139/probe-driver-version-drift.py` (8/8 today; after a restart expect cell A to go RED and the next log line to carry `(pass N)` and `[model: ...]`).

**IF restart-loop-driver IS TICKED:** re-run that probe as the in-situ confirmation, record that the driver is current, and note in the done entry which of the two commits' behaviours you can now SEE in the log (the `(pass N)` field and the state.json-derived iteration number). Nothing else needs doing — no code change is pending, the code is already correct.

**IF ANY OTHER SIDE ITEM IS TICKED OR decisions.formatOnEditHook IS SET:** GATES.md carries the exact follow-up for each, and the loop's half is the same shape every time — the paste lands in a file the loop cannot write, so `git add` it (iter89 committed `.claude/references/` that way), then re-run that item's probe as the in-situ confirmation: paste-format-on-edit-hook -> .mtk/paths-133/probe-project-settings-hook.py (expect the 127 gone); paste-force-push-hook -> `git push deny-probe-nonexistent-remote HEAD --force`, which cannot reach a real remote, and expect the hook's §8.2 refusal. For formatOnEditHook "delete", the `hooks` key comes out and tools/hooks/format-on-edit.py is deleted with it.

**IF NOTHING IS TICKED:** re-run the two liveness probes (~10 s each: `python3 .mtk/paths-121/probe-labels.py`, `python3 .mtk/paths-113/verify-space.py`), then end WAITING-GATE. That is the honest ending. iters 126-139 all took it and EVERY ITERATION WILL UNTIL A BOX IS TICKED. Do not invent work to avoid it.

**READ tools/loop/method-notes.md BEFORE WRITING A PROBE OR A TEST**, and **USE `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py --find <n>` TO READ AN ITERATION OUT OF THE ARCHIVE** — it resolves both entry shapes (a bare grep is wrong for 27 of them, iter136) and also prints that iteration's transcript path, which for anything before iter137 is filed under a DIFFERENT number. THIS FILE'S BUDGET HEADROOM is in method-notes too, and it is TIGHT.

**THE CLASS OF WORK THAT IS STILL LEGITIMATE WHEN THE FEATURE BACKLOG IS EMPTY: run the protocol literally and report what does not work.** 126-133: the dead phone-push channel, the two step-1 Read ceilings, the checker measuring one of three files, §8.2 covering one spelling of force-push, the unread CLI stderr, the red suite at HEAD, the dead format-on-edit hook, the archive missing iter132. 134: ci.yml red on the runner it had never run on. 135: that runner never installing the renderer. 136: the archive's own lookup instruction. 137: the driver's iteration number. 138: the size guard's own safety argument, inverted. 139: the driver itself, 56.6 h stale, with 137's fix inside it never executing. THE BOUNDARY, and hold it: this licence covers the loop's own machinery — the files the protocol reads, the channels it claims, the checks and guards it relies on. It does NOT license inventing feature work or a sixth PLAN.md sweep.

**THERE IS NO LEAD LEFT.** iter139 spent the standing invitation and closed it. DO NOT MANUFACTURE A REPLACEMENT. With no lead and no ticked box, the honest increment is the two liveness probes and WAITING-GATE. If you want somewhere to look, the invitation is unchanged and has now paid out fourteen times: pick a thing the protocol CLAIMS and measure whether it is true. **A pattern worth noticing from 133/138/139: the richest finds were all places where a failure is SWALLOWED BY CONSTRUCTION** — a PostToolUse hook whose exit code never reaches the agent, a size guard whose docstring asserted its own safety, `notify()` discarding both streams and its exit code. Grep for `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`, and bare `except:` in the loop's own machinery before you look anywhere else.

THE PATTERN IS THE POINT: the iteration that grows this file pays it back, rather than raising the budget to suit itself. ASSERT THE ENTRY YOU DROP IS ALREADY IN THE ARCHIVE before dropping it, and run `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` afterwards.
